name: Samsung Pyeongtaek P2

process_nodes.label: 1z DRAM
process_nodes.note: Third-generation 10nm-class DRAM made with EUV; the line's first product was 16Gb LPDDR5 mobile DRAM.

process_nodes.label: 5nm
process_nodes.note: The EUV foundry line Samsung began building at Pyeongtaek in May 2020 targets 5nm and finer; Samsung's August 2020 release says Line 2 would add foundry output after DRAM, and Korea JoongAng Daily placed the foundry equipment in P2.

summary: Samsung's second production line at its Pyeongtaek campus in Gyeonggi Province, which Samsung described as the largest-scale chip production line to date, saying it spans more than 128,900 m² (about 16 football pitches) without saying whether that is land, floor or cleanroom area. Mass production of 16Gb LPDDR5 mobile DRAM on Samsung's EUV-based 1z process began there in August 2020, and Samsung said the line would go on to make V-NAND and foundry chips. Construction of an EUV foundry line for 5nm-and-finer logic and of a V-NAND facility inside Line 2 began in May 2020, both aimed at the second half of 2021. By September 2022 P2 was making DRAM, NAND flash and EUV-based processors, and Samsung put the amount invested in it at more than KRW 30 trillion.

metrics.note: Amount Samsung said had gone into P2 alone.

milestones.note: Construction of the EUV foundry line began in May 2020.
Cleanroom construction for the NAND line began in May 2020.
Samsung announced on 30 August 2020 that mass production of 16Gb LPDDR5 DRAM had begun on the line.

notes: Samsung's May 2020 foundry release does not name the line; its August 2020 release says Line 2 would produce foundry chips after DRAM, and its June 2020 NAND release places the new V-NAND facility inside Line 2. The 300 mm wafer size follows from the May 2020 release, which says the new Pyeongtaek line brings Samsung's foundry network to six 12-inch lines and one 8-inch line. The cited sources do not give dates when the foundry and NAND lines reached mass production. The 128,900 m² that Samsung gives for Line 2 is not recorded as a site or cleanroom area because the release does not say which area it measures.

review.method: Independent AI-assisted review (Claude): re-opened every cited source, checked each statement against it and searched for newer reporting.
review.changes: Corrected the notes and summary, which said only Korean press placed the foundry and NAND lines in P2; Samsung's own June and August 2020 releases place them in Line 2. Removed a news source from the foundry construction milestone it did not support and reworded the summary. Audit fixes (2026-11-07): Reworded the summary to say Samsung's release gives the 128,900 m² as the area the line spans without saying whether it is land, floor or cleanroom area, and noted why it is not recorded as a figure.
